overall.recognizable_route_precision_reason: Undefined because the denominator is zero: no response proposed any of the five routes.

blind_response_characterization.description: Most outputs are repeated gear symbols, MethodManager placeholders, or other nonsemantic fragments. The few English fragments propose score addition or a generic equality predicate, neither of which is one of the five routes.

same_elements: The same five route definitions were used.
The response's actually proposed method controlled the label; intended or correct methods were never supplied.
Ambiguous or missing outputs were explicitly labeled and counted incorrect after unblinding.
Judgments and their hash were sealed before joining to the same 100 gold route and matched-pair records.
Overall, per-route, matched-pair, and recognizable-route precision use the same formulas.
protocol_comparison_to_iter035.difference: This iter014 audit was intentionally stricter before sealing: only response text was available. The iter035 audit task allowed the public prompt for reference resolution. Therefore only protocol, not conclusions or numerical outcomes, should be compared directly.

limitations: The response-only blind condition is conservative: no prompt context was used to resolve vague references.
Recognizable-route precision is mathematically undefined, not zero, because there are no recognizable route predictions.
This is a single-auditor semantic classification, although the pervasive nonsemantic degeneration leaves little interpretive latitude.
The audit measures method selection only, not problem solving or proof correctness.
No causal conclusion about training changes should be drawn from this audit alone; generation and evaluation conditions must be compared separately.
